measured.on: the SAP sandbox (ABAP release 758), as a client, through RFC-enabled probe modules of our own; every object deleted afterwards

flags.X_K1: fill K1 with its initial value literally
flags.X_K2: fill K2 with its initial value literally

isolation: Every case starts with fresh sessions for each owner it names and an empty lock table for ZOSD_PRB; nothing carries over from an earlier case. On the sandbox each case used its own key values and ended with DEQUEUE_ALL of every owner (and the end of the O2 session), so NUMBER and the rows of each read depend only on the case's own steps.

schema.steps: run in order; a step completes before the next starts unless it has async
schema.expect: the gate: what the system answered
schema.observed: informational: what the sandbox showed, not a gate (elapsed times, reads whose result depends on a race)
schema.informational: true on a step that is not a gate at all; its result is in observed
schema.expect.eventuallyWithinMs: on a read: the rows must be reached within this many ms of the previous step's completion (poll); release here is asynchronous
schema.expect.elapsedMs: a tolerant bound {min,max} on the step's duration in ms
schema.expect.grantedWithinMsOfRelease: a _WAIT request is granted no later than this many ms after the conflicting lock went
schema.async: {delayMs, relativeTo}: the step fires delayMs after the next step starts, without waiting for it
schema.END_SESSION: the owner's session ends (RFC connection closed, task or job ended); its locks of every scope go, asynchronously -- except locks already handed to an update task by COMMIT WORK, which stay until the update has run
schema.expect.newUpdateOwner: on a COMMIT WORK or ROLLBACK WORK step: true = the session's next _SCOPE 2 lock carries a different GUSRVB than its locks before the step; false = the same one. Absent = not measured
schema.GUSRVB <S>^: the update owner that session S handed to its update task at its last COMMIT WORK; the update task holds those locks, and to every session including S they are another owner's (601)
schema.CALL FUNCTION <update module> IN UPDATE: params.durationMs: how long the V1 update module takes; the steps between its COMMIT WORK and the next eventually-read run inside that window

owners.O1: the calling session: a stateful RFC connection; its locks outlive each call on that connection
owners.O2: a second session: synchronous CALL FUNCTION ... DESTINATION 'NONE' from O1; stateful until RFC_CONNECTION_CLOSE
owners.O3: a third session that stays open until an END_SESSION step for it (or the end of the case). On the sandbox it was CALL FUNCTION ... STARTING NEW TASK ... DESTINATION 'NONE' of a module that enqueued and then waited (WAIT UP TO n SECONDS, 3 s in dequeue-all-not-others, 2 s in wait-released) before returning; its session ended when the module returned. Its ENQUEUE had completed before O1's next step (O1 waited 1 s after starting the task), and every read that shows its lock fell inside the wait.
owners.OJ: a background job: SUBMIT ... VIA JOB + JOB_CLOSE strtimmed; its session ends when its program ends (END_SESSION)
owners.model: a session has two owner ids. GUSR (dialog owner) holds _SCOPE 1 and lives as long as the session; GUSRVB (update owner) holds _SCOPE 2 and is replaced after a ROLLBACK WORK and after a COMMIT WORK that ran an update. _SCOPE 3 is one row carrying both. In expect, GUSR/GUSRVB name the session whose owner id it is; null = blank.

notation.\uffff: ENQUEUE_READ returns U+FFFF in every character position of a field that was locked generically (initial value, X_<field> not set)
notation.GARG: client + K1 (10) + K2 (10); trailing blanks are not significant
notation.<USER>: the user name of the holder (sy-msgv1); all sessions ran as one user
notation.K2: an ENQUEUE step without K2 in the case text uses K2='K'; an empty K2 is the initial value
notation.rows: ENQUEUE_READ (GNAME = 'ZOSD_PRB', GUNAME = space); row order is not part of the contract
notation.MC 601 / 602: 601 = held by another owner, 602 = refused against the caller's own lock; both raise FOREIGN_LOCK with sy-msgv1 = the user. When a request collides with both, the conflicting lock acquired first decides (group 2b). Observed, not gated: sy-msgv2 = the lock object name on a refusal

enqueueRead.note: observations, outside the gate: the parameter and field types as the interface declared them, the owner-id format and the values seen. Cases gate only GARG, GMODE, GUSE, GUSEVB, NUMBER and which session's id GUSR / GUSRVB is.
enqueueRead.ownerId: 58 characters: a 20-digit timestamp (YYYYMMDDhhmmss + 6 digits), 4 digits, 2 digits, then the application server instance name, padded with '.'. Compare for equality only; do not parse.
